intro.organize: Rebuild a PDF the way you want it: drag pages into a new order, rotate them, insert blank pages, or pull pages in from another file. Handy when a scan comes back in the wrong order.
intro.merge: Combine several PDFs into a single document, in exactly the order you choose. Drag the files to fix the sequence before you export.
intro.split: Cut one PDF into several files. Insert break points where the splits should happen, then export only the parts you need.
intro.rotate: Fix pages that were scanned sideways or upside down. Rotate the selected pages by 90° or 180°, or mirror them horizontally and vertically.
intro.reorderPages: Change the page order of a PDF on a visual grid: drag page cards around, rotate single pages, then export them in the new sequence.
intro.deletePages: Remove unwanted pages from a PDF. Click the pages you want to delete, or use the odd/even shortcut and the range field on long documents.
intro.extractPages: Pull selected pages out of a PDF and export them as one new document, or as a ZIP of single-page files.
intro.crop: Trim margins or cut to a region on every page with eight drag handles. Apply the crop to the whole document, odd or even pages, or just the pages you select.
intro.edit: Add text boxes, white-out blocks and a handwritten signature to a PDF, then download the edited file.
intro.pdfToImage: Turn PDF pages into high-resolution PNG, JPG or WebP images. Choose the resolution you need, up to 300 DPI, then download single pages or the whole set as a ZIP.
intro.imageToPdf: Build a single PDF from PNG, JPG or WebP images. Drag the images into order and set the page size, orientation and margin.
intro.compress: Make a PDF smaller without sending it anywhere. The lossless level repacks the file and keeps the text selectable; the image levels can halve a scan, at the cost of turning its pages into pictures.

useCases.heading: Common ways to use it
organize: Put a scanned contract back into the right page order before sending it out.
Add blank pages for notes or for double-sided printing.
Combine the best pages of several drafts into one clean document.
merge: Join invoices or receipts into one file for bookkeeping.
Combine a cover letter, CV and references into a single application PDF.
Assemble a report from chapters exported as separate PDFs.
split: Extract just one chapter from a long manual.
Separate a scanned batch into one file per person.
Send only the signed pages of a contract.
rotate: Fix phone photos of documents that were saved sideways.
Turn landscape tables back to portrait for printing.
Correct pages from a scanner that fed paper upside down.
reorderPages: Move a misplaced page to the front of a report.
Reverse the order of a scan that came out backwards.
Put appendix pages at the end after assembling a document.
deletePages: Remove blank pages left by double-sided scanning.
Drop outdated price sheets before sending a catalogue.
Strip internal draft pages from a client-facing document.
extractPages: Save only the price table from a long proposal.
Pull the signed page out of a contract for your records.
Export diagram pages for a slide deck.
crop: Trim the black border left by a scanner.
Cut a PDF to A4 or Letter after printing to PDF.
Remove a footer or sidebar that should not be printed.
edit: Fill in a form that is not interactive.
Add a signature on a device without a printer.
White out an old address before sharing a document.
pdfToImage: Use PDF pages in a presentation or on a website.
Post a page preview on social media.

imageToPdf: Turn phone photos of documents into one PDF.
Collect scanned receipts into a single expense file.

Scanned contracts and reports kept on a phone with little storage.
Upload portals that reject a CV or an invoice above 5 MB.

detail.organize: Use the organizer when the document itself is fine and only the sequence is wrong: a scan stitched from two passes, a contract whose signature page ended up at the back, a proposal with the appendix in the middle. Unlike merging, nothing is combined here, so the page count only changes when you add blank pages or pull pages in from another file.
detail.merge: Merging fits when the information already lives in separate files and belongs in one: a folder of supplier invoices, chapters exported one by one, a contract plus its annex. Every page keeps its original size, so mixing A4 and Letter is allowed but looks uneven once printed.
detail.split: Split is for handing over part of a document without exposing the rest: one chapter to a reviewer, a single invoice to accounting, the signed pages to a counterparty. Break points sit between pages, so if a section starts in the middle of a page, crop it first and split the result.
detail.rotate: Rotate is a repair tool: it changes orientation and nothing else. A sheet fed upside down, a photo of a form saved sideways, a landscape table inside a portrait report. Only a rotation flag is written, so the text stays selectable and the file size does not change.
detail.reorderPages: The page editor is for re-sequencing a document you already have: every page appears as a thumbnail, which makes a missing or duplicated scan easy to spot. It works on one file at a time; when the pages come from several documents, use organize or merge instead.
detail.deletePages: Reach for delete when a document is mostly right but carries pages that should not travel with it: a blank reverse side, a superseded quote, an internal cover sheet. Nothing is written until you export, so an accidental removal costs nothing more than reloading the file.
detail.extractPages: Extract is the inverse of delete: instead of removing pages you keep only the ones you name. Pull an invoice out of a statement, an annex out of a contract, a chapter out of a manual — as one new PDF or as a ZIP with one file per page.
detail.crop: Cropping narrows the visible area without rewriting the page, so text inside the frame stays selectable. It is the honest fix for a scanner border, an over-wide slide export or a browser header baked in by print-to-PDF; whatever sits outside the frame is hidden rather than deleted, which is why the file size barely moves.
detail.edit: The editor covers small additions to a finished PDF: filling a field on a non-interactive form, signing without a printer, covering an old address before a document is forwarded. It does not reflow text — additions sit on top of the page, so a long replacement sentence may not fit the space the original occupied.
detail.pdfToImage: Convert to an image when the destination cannot display a PDF: a chat app, a slide deck, a CMS upload field. Rendering happens at the resolution you choose, so 150 DPI suits screens and chat, 300 DPI is what print and OCR want, and higher settings only inflate the file.
detail.imageToPdf: Image-to-PDF is the return trip: photos of receipts, exported design frames, screenshots of a conversation. Because each page is built from an image, the exported file has no searchable text — run OCR on the result if the document has to be indexed or quoted.
detail.compress: Use this when a PDF is too heavy to send or store and you can accept a trade-off. Lossless rewriting only repacks the file structure: text stays selectable and nothing visible changes, but a document exported by recent software has little redundancy left, so a few percent is a normal outcome. The image levels re-render every page as a JPEG, which is what actually shrinks a scan and also what turns its text into a picture. Compress the copy you are about to print or attach and keep the original for anything you may still need to search or edit.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How Reeff.PDF handles your files and data: every tool runs in your browser and your PDFs are never uploaded.
privacy.intro: Reeff.PDF (pdf.reeff.app) is a free set of browser-based PDF tools. This page explains what happens to your files, and what limited information we and our partners process when you use the site.
privacy.contactLabel: Questions about this policy or your data? Write to us:

sections.heading: Your files never leave your device
sections.body: Every PDF and image you open is read, edited and saved by code running inside your browser. There is no upload step and no server-side processing: your documents are never sent to us or to anyone else.

sections.heading: What our servers see
sections.body: There are no accounts and no storage for your files, their names or their contents — nothing ever arrives to be stored. Like any website, requests reach our host (Cloudflare), which keeps short-lived technical logs such as IP address, browser and page requested in order to deliver pages and block abuse. We look at aggregate, non-identifying figures (page views per tool and per language) to decide what to improve.

sections.heading: Cookies and local storage
sections.body: The tools work without cookies. Your browser may keep small preferences locally, such as the language you picked. Where advertising is enabled, our advertising partners may set their own cookies or read device identifiers; see the next section.

sections.heading: Advertising and Google AdSense
sections.body: The site is free because it is supported by ads. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this and other websites. Google's use of advertising cookies lets it and its partners show you ads based on your visits. You can opt out of personalised advertising in Google Ads Settings at https://www.google.com/settings/ads or at https://www.aboutads.info/choices. Visitors in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland are asked for consent before any advertising cookie is set.

sections.heading: Third-party services
sections.body: We rely on Cloudflare for hosting, DNS and content delivery, and — when ads are shown — on Google and its partners for advertising. Those companies handle data under their own privacy policies. Links to other websites are outside our control.

sections.heading: Children
sections.body: The service is not directed at children under 13 (16 in the EEA and the UK), and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

sections.heading: Your rights and changes to this policy
sections.body: We do not keep personal data of our own, so access, correction or deletion requests usually concern our host or advertising partners; write to us and we will help you route them. If you are in the EEA, the UK, California or another region with data-protection law, you can contact us at any time. We update this page when our practices change, and the date above always shows the current version.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.description: The terms that apply when you use the free browser-based PDF tools on Reeff.PDF.
terms.intro: These terms cover your use of Reeff.PDF (pdf.reeff.app). By using the site you accept them, so please read them first.
terms.contactLabel: Questions about these terms? Write to us:

sections.heading: The service
sections.body: Reeff.PDF is a free collection of tools that read, edit and save PDF files inside your browser. It is offered as it is, needs no account, and may gain features, change or be discontinued at any time.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: You may use the tools for personal or commercial document work. You may not use them for content you have no right to handle, for anything unlawful, or to attack the service — for example automated scraping, attempts to exhaust our bandwidth, or interference with other users.

sections.heading: Your files and content
sections.body: Whatever you open in the tools stays yours. We claim no licence over your documents and no ownership of them, and because they never reach us we could not inspect them even in principle.

sections.heading: No warranty
sections.body: The tools are provided without warranty of any kind. PDF rendering and editing can be imperfect: keep a copy of the original file and check the result before relying on it for anything important.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
sections.body: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for lost data, lost profits or indirect damages resulting from the use of, or the inability to use, this site. Nothing here limits rights you have under mandatory consumer law.

sections.heading: Advertising
sections.body: The service is free and funded by advertising. Ads come from third parties and their content is not endorsed by us. Blocking them is technically possible, but it removes the support that keeps the project running.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
sections.body: We may update these terms; the date above shows the current version and continued use after a change means you accept it. Questions? Write to us below.

free.a: Yes. Every tool is free and unlimited: no account, no watermark, no page or file cap.

privacy.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
privacy.a: No. The tools run entirely in your browser, so your PDF never leaves your device.

sizeLimit.q: Is there a file size limit?
sizeLimit.a: There is no cap imposed by us. Very large files are limited only by your device's memory and browser.

mobile.q: Does it work on a phone or tablet?
mobile.a: Yes. The tools work in current mobile browsers; larger documents are simply easier on a desktop.

organize.q: Can I mix pages from different PDFs?
organize.a: Yes. While organizing you can pull pages in from another file and place them anywhere in the new order.

merge.q: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
merge.a: As many as you like. There is no file-count limit; only your device's memory matters.

split.q: Can I split a PDF into single pages?
split.a: Yes. Choose the separate-pages option to export every page as its own file, delivered as a ZIP.

rotate.q: Does rotating change the page content?
rotate.a: No. Only the page orientation changes; text, images and quality stay exactly the same.

reorderPages.q: Can I move several pages at once?
reorderPages.a: You drag pages one by one, and you can select a range before applying a rotation or an export.

deletePages.q: Can I undo a deleted page?
deletePages.a: Yes — nothing is written until you export. Deselect the page or reopen the file to bring it back.

extractPages.q: Which format do extracted pages come in?
extractPages.a: Choose one new PDF containing all selected pages, or a ZIP with one PDF per page.

crop.a: You decide: apply the crop to the whole document, odd or even pages, or only the pages you select.

edit.a: You can cover it with a white-out block. The original text is not reflowed, so the layout stays intact.

pdfToImage.q: What resolution can I export at?
pdfToImage.a: Up to 300 DPI. A higher DPI means sharper images and larger files.

imageToPdf.a: PNG, JPG and WebP. Other formats are converted in your browser before the PDF is built.

compress.q: Will compressing make the text blurry?
compress.a: On the lossless level, no: only the file structure is rewritten, so text and images are untouched. The image levels do lower the resolution, which is exactly what makes them work — check the result before you delete the original.

organize.q: Does reorganizing reduce the file quality?
organize.a: No. Pages are copied as they are, so text, images and resolution stay identical; only the order and any inserted blank pages differ.

organize.q: Can I organize a password-protected PDF?
organize.a: You have to unlock it first. Showing a preview means reading every page, and an encrypted document cannot be read without its password.

merge.q: Are page sizes normalised when files are merged?
merge.a: No. Each page keeps its own dimensions, so A4 and Letter can sit in the same document and still print at their original sizes.

merge.q: What happens to bookmarks after merging?
merge.a: Page content is preserved in full, but document-level bookmarks are not carried into the new file; they have to be added again.

split.q: How are the split files named?
split.a: The original file name plus a part number, packaged in one ZIP so a single download delivers every part.

split.q: What happens to pages no break point covers?
split.a: They stay in their own part and are never dropped; only the boundaries you place between pages cut the document.

rotate.q: Can I rotate only one page of many?
rotate.a: Yes. Rotation is stored per page, so you can straighten a single sideways sheet and leave the rest untouched.
No. The page content is not re-rendered, so resolution, fonts and images are identical before and after.

reorderPages.q: Does it work on very long documents?
reorderPages.a: Thumbnails are rendered in the browser, so a file with several hundred pages takes a moment to fill in — most noticeably on a phone.

reorderPages.q: Can I rotate a page while reordering?
reorderPages.a: Yes. Rotation is stored per page, so one crooked scan can be corrected without affecting the others.

deletePages.q: Can I delete a whole range at once?
deletePages.a: Use the range field for a block such as 4-12, or the odd/even shortcut to strip every other page from a two-sided scan.

deletePages.q: Does deleting pages make the file smaller?
deletePages.a: Yes. Removed pages are not written to the export at all, so cutting a 200-page file down to 20 pages shrinks it considerably.

extractPages.q: Can the extracted pages be reordered?
extractPages.a: They keep their original order. If you need a different sequence, run the result through the page editor afterwards.

extractPages.q: Is text still selectable in the extracted pages?
extractPages.a: Yes. Pages are copied rather than re-rendered, so text, fonts and annotations survive intact.

crop.q: Is the cropped area really gone?
crop.a: It no longer prints and no longer shows, because the visible page box is narrowed. The underlying content is not rewritten, which is why the file size hardly changes.

crop.q: Can different pages be cropped differently?
crop.a: Yes. Apply one frame to the whole document, or switch to the selected pages so each keeps its own crop.

edit.a: Yes. Draw or type a signature once, then place it on as many pages as the document needs.
No. Additions are layered over the page, so original text cannot be selected or rewritten — cover it with a white-out block if it has to disappear.

pdfToImage.a: 150 for screens and chat, 200 for slides, 300 for print or OCR. Higher values look sharper and make the files much larger.

pdfToImage.q: Can I convert only some pages?
pdfToImage.a: Yes. Export every page or only the ones you select, either as single downloads or as one ZIP.

imageToPdf.a: They are embedded without a second round of compression, so sharp photos stay sharp and the PDF grows with them — that is expected.

imageToPdf.q: Can one PDF mix page sizes?
imageToPdf.a: The size you pick applies to the whole batch. For mixed formats, build two PDFs and merge them so each page keeps its own size.

compress.q: Why did my file shrink so little?
compress.a: Lossless compression can only remove redundancy in how the file is stored. A modern tool has little left to remove, so a few percent is a normal result, not a failure.

compress.q: Does compressing remove metadata or permissions?
compress.a: The lossless level leaves both as they are. The image levels rebuild the document from rendered pages, so old metadata and permission flags do not carry over — handy for a scan that still names whoever scanned it.

about.title: About these PDF tools
about.description: Reeff.PDF is a free set of browser-based PDF tools for office chores — what it does, what it deliberately leaves out, and how it stays free.
about.intro: Reeff.PDF is one of the Reeff office tools: PDF chores you can finish inside the browser, without installing anything, creating an account, or waiting for a file to travel to a server and back.

sections.heading: What this site is
sections.body: Twelve tools for the PDF chores that actually come up in an office: putting pages in order, merging, splitting, rotating, deleting, extracting, cropping, editing text, compressing a file, and converting to and from images. Each one does a single job on a single page, with no settings panel to learn first.

sections.heading: Why it is built this way
sections.body: The whole job — open the file, change it, save it — happens inside your browser, so it finishes at the speed of your own machine instead of your upload speed. That also means no queue, no daily quota, and nothing left behind on a server to clean up afterwards.

sections.heading: What it deliberately does not do
sections.body: There is no cloud storage, no account history, no text recognition for scanned pages, no e-signature and no AI summary. All of those need a server, and adding them quietly would break the promise above; if one ever arrives it is marked with a badge on its page, and the local tools stay local.

sections.heading: How it is paid for
sections.body: The tools that run in the browser are free and unlimited. A few pages carry advertising, and any future feature that needs a server is priced per use rather than through a metered free tier. No countdown timers, and no free feature quietly moved behind a payment.

howItWorks.title: How these PDF tools work
howItWorks.description: Where your file goes when you pick a tool, what "runs locally" actually means, which steps need the internet, and how large a PDF a browser can handle.
howItWorks.intro: Every Reeff.PDF tool follows the same three steps, and none of them uploads your document.

steps.title: Pick a tool
steps.body: Open the page for the job you have at hand. It loads like any other web page: no extension, no desktop program, no sign-up form.

steps.title: Your browser does the work
steps.body: The page downloads the code that reads and rewrites PDFs, and that code runs on your own device. Your file is read from disk into memory and never leaves the tab.

steps.title: Save the result
steps.body: The edited document is produced in memory and handed back to your browser as a download. Close the tab and nothing is left anywhere — there was never a copy on a server to delete.

sections.heading: "Runs locally" means no upload request
sections.body: When you choose a file, the browser reads it from your disk instead of posting it to an endpoint, so there is no transfer to wait for and no size limit set by a server. The practical ceiling is your device's memory: a few hundred pages is comfortable on a laptop, while a long scanned document on a phone will feel noticeably slower.

sections.heading: When a step needs the internet
sections.body: The page itself has to load once, and switching language needs a connection too. After that, an open tool keeps working with the network switched off. Any future feature that genuinely needs a server — cloud OCR, for example — is labelled as needing internet on its own page instead of being described as local.

sections.heading: Files and browsers it handles
sections.body: Recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on desktop and mobile. Password-protected PDFs open once you type the password; scanned pages are treated as images, so text inside them cannot be selected or edited. Everything the tools produce is a standard PDF that opens anywhere.

upload.prompt: Click or drag a PDF file here to make it smaller
upload.hint: Lossless keeps the text selectable; the image levels shrink scans the most

levels.label: Compression level
levels.lightBody: Rewrites the file structure. Text stays selectable — expect a few percent.
levels.balancedBody: Renders each page at 150 DPI as JPEG. Text becomes an image.
levels.strongBody: 110 DPI at lower quality. Smallest result, softest text.

result.heading: Result
result.notSmaller: This file cannot get smaller at this level: the result is the same size or larger, so there is nothing to download. Try Balanced or Strong if you really need it under a limit.
result.rasterNote: Every page is now a picture. Keep the original if you may need to search, select or edit the text later.
result.losslessNote: The text was not touched — it is still selectable and searchable.

warning.heavy: Large files take a while to render. Keep this tab open; you can cancel between pages.

errors.encrypted: This PDF is password-protected. Open it once with its password, save an unlocked copy, then compress that.
errors.readFailed: This file could not be read as a PDF. Please try another one.
errors.compressFailed: Something went wrong while compressing. The original file is untouched.
